_comment: Rules consumed by periodica.get (Rust core: rust/periodica_core/src/rules.rs) - all data-driven, no hardcoded chemistry. Edit this file to extend the system to new tiers or property arithmetic without touching code.
_tier_comment: Every folder under data/active/ is a curated tier. Tiers whose name matches a data/derived/<name>/ folder merge into one registry tier; within a merged tier the curated filename stem outranks a derived Symbol, so hand-written sheets win by name while derived entries stay reachable by symbol.
_integral_properties_comment: Additive properties that are integral quantum numbers. A composed total within 1e-9 of an integer is snapped to it (quark charges are stored as 0.6666666667). No other property is ever snapped: masses keep their exact sum.
_resolution_levels_comment: How an unscoped brace spec picks its constituents. Each level is a group of tiers; the first level in which every constituent symbol matches exactly (case-sensitive) resolves the whole spec, so {N=1,H=3} is ammonia from atoms while {P=1,N=0,E=1} is hydrogen from particles. If no level covers the spec, each symbol must resolve unambiguously on its own; a symbol naming different entries in different tiers raises AmbiguousConstituent. Scoped specs (from_=...) ignore this list.
_mass_sources_comment: Curated masses for generated tiers (build time only: scripts/build_*.py compose an entry, then take Mass_amu from the declared reference and derive Mass_MeVc2 and Mass_kg with the CODATA 2018 factors below; the registry serves the generated files). element = CIAAW 2021 standard atomic weight of element Z (abridged value for interval elements; AME2020 nuclide mass when CIAAW gives none). nuclide = AME2020 atomic mass of nuclide (Z, A). Both are neutral-atom masses; entries whose electron count differs from Z are corrected by that many electron masses.
_refinements_comment: Applied in order by periodica.refine after every composition, so that
Get() on a spec and the saved JSON built from that spec always agree.
Each refiner is a no-op for specs it does not apply to, so the list is
unconditional. Emptying this list restores raw additive composition.

refinements._why: Summed free-nucleon mass is ~1% too high for every nucleus; the semi-empirical mass formula supplies the missing mass defect.
Constituent JSON has no Mass_kg, so additive composition reported Mass_kg: 0 -- a zero that reads as a measurement.
A composed atom otherwise carries no measurable property at all. Join it to the curated elements tier on atomic number.
